clue.text: Short skirts irritate clerics

definitions.note: a collective: the ministry is the body of clergy

parts.note: minis are short skirts, miniskirts
to try someone is to irritate them, as in trying their patience

explanation.surface: Clergy are annoyed by women wearing miniskirts.
explanation.definitionFit: The ministry is the clergy taken as a body, so it stands for clerics collectively.

clue.text: Half-time count only

indicators.note: half of the word time is taken here, its second half

parts.note: to count on someone is to rely on them, so count can mean rely

explanation.surface: At half-time a tally is taken, and nothing more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half' takes the second half of 'time', ME; the hyphen in 'Half-time' hides that split.
explanation.definitionFit: Merely and only are synonyms, both meaning no more than, simply.

clue.text: Observe the over-weight get really cold

indicators.note: over signals turning the word for weight upside down, so it is read backwards

parts.note: a ton is a unit of weight
to ice is to freeze, to become very cold

explanation.surface: Watch the overweight person catch a real chill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over-weight' reads as fat, but 'over' turns TON round to NOT.
explanation.definitionFit: To notice something is to observe it, to see and register it.

clue.text: Point to a mad character responsible for smash

parts.note: S, south, is a compass point
the Mad Hatter of Alice in Wonderland; 'mad as a hatter'

explanation.surface: Someone singles out a lunatic as the one who broke things.
explanation.definitionFit: To shatter something is to smash it to pieces.

clue.text: Pity the woman!

definitions.meaning: an old word for pity or compassion, surviving in ruthless
A woman's name, also a biblical heroine

explanation.definitionFit: An archaic noun for compassion, and also a girl's name, as in the Book of Ruth.

clue.text: Husband — a little egghead

parts.note: a scrap is a small piece, a little of something

indicators.note: the head of the word egg is its first letter

explanation.surface: A married man is described as a minor intellectual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Husband' is a verb here, to economise, not a married man; 'egghead' splits as egg + head, the first letter of egg.
explanation.definitionFit: To husband resources is to use them sparingly, to save and scrimp.

clue.text: Turned up with a group to see King Arthur's residence

parts.note: came is a synonym of turned up, arrived
a lot is a group or batch of things

explanation.surface: Someone arrived with a party to visit the legendary king's court.
explanation.definitionFit: In legend Camelot is the castle and court where King Arthur lived.

clue.text: A large number prefer no-one to back the take-over

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, a large number
to opt is to choose, to prefer

indicators.note: to back means the preceding word is read backwards

parts.note: no is NO and one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A big crowd would rather nobody supported the corporate takeover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to back' turns NOI round to ION, completing OPTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoption is taking over something as one's own, a child, a policy or an idea.

clue.text: Tips out of metres possibly

parts.note: ex is Latin for out of, as in ex-works

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of metres could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Advice drawn from measurements in metres, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges METRES into TREMES after EX.
explanation.definitionFit: Extremes are the furthest ends of something, its tips or limits.

clue.text: Withdraws touching brochures

parts.note: re means concerning, touching on
tracts are pamphlets or leaflets

explanation.surface: Someone pulls out of a deal concerning leaflets.
explanation.definitionFit: To retract is to take back or pull in, so retracts means withdraws.

clue.text: Bring in a representative or split it

indicators.note: split says the word it is broken open with other letters put inside

parts.note: MP, Member of Parliament, is an elected representative

explanation.surface: Introduce an agent or else divide the thing up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'split' cuts IT open to take MP and OR.
explanation.definitionFit: To import goods is to bring them in from abroad.

clue.text: Following study, have an inclination to argue

indicators.note: following places the inclination word after the study word

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
to tend is to be inclined or disposed

explanation.surface: After some reading, someone feels like having a row.
explanation.definitionFit: To contend is to assert or maintain in debate, to argue.

clue.text: Company returns in modern place

indicators.note: in puts the reversed company abbreviation inside the word for modern

parts.note: late can mean recent, as in the latest model

indicators.note: returns means the abbreviation for company comes back the other way

explanation.surface: A firm comes back to a contemporary venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns CO into OC, which goes inside LATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To locate something is to place or site it, to fix its position.

clue.text: Profligate cut by a European, though game

indicators.note: cut by means the word for a profligate is split with the European inside

parts.note: a roue is a dissolute, profligate man
a Lett is a Latvian, someone from a Baltic country

explanation.surface: A rake is wounded by a foreigner, yet still has some fight in him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' reads as plucky in the surface but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Roulette is a casino gambling game played on a spinning wheel.

clue.text: Depletion of capital assets

parts.note: read in finance, a cut in the value of assets; read with capital as head, a trim of the locks on top

explanation.definitionFit: In finance a haircut is a reduction in an asset's value; literally it removes hair, the head's assets.

clue.text: Crooked brokers state there's a way to stay on top and get along

definitions.text: a way to stay on top and get along

indicators.note: crooked says the letters of the two words are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: Dishonest dealers say there is a method of staying ahead and surviving.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a swimming stroke, which keeps you on the surface of the water and moves you forward.

clue.text: A bit over-excited, so unsuccessful

indicators.note: excited says the letters are stirred up into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Slightly too worked up, and so a failure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over-excited' reads as one word, but 'excited' rearranges A, BIT and OVER.
explanation.definitionFit: An abortive attempt is one that comes to nothing, a failure.

clue.text: Stick together, given cash present

parts.note: coin is money in metal form, cash
here means present, in attendance

explanation.surface: Bound together, since the money is in hand.
explanation.definitionFit: To cohere or coinhere is to be united, to cleave together.

clue.text: A monk acting as advocate makes the connection

parts.note: a brother is a member of a religious order, a monk
someone practising as an advocate is in law, working in the legal profession

explanation.surface: A friar working as a lawyer forges a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A relative by marriage is a family connection.

clue.text: There's work at last for listing

definitions.meaning: a cobbler shapes shoes on a last; fitting new heels is that work
a ship that leans to one side is ... over

explanation.definitionFit: Repairing shoe heels is a cobbler's job at the last; a ship tilting sideways heels.

clue.text: A second showing no heart maybe

indicators.note: maybe says the letters might be arranged differently

explanation.surface: Someone displays a lack of feeling, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Another means one more of the same kind, a second one.

clue.text: A judge or military leader effecting some improvement

parts.note: a ref, referee, judges a match

indicators.note: the leader of military is its first letter

explanation.surface: An official or army commander brings about some change for the better.
explanation.definitionFit: A reform is a change made to put things right, an improvement.

clue.text: Many get ready to do battle in French opera

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100, many
to arm is to equip for war
en is French for in

explanation.surface: Many prepare to fight in a French opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French opera' reads together, but 'in French' gives EN.
explanation.definitionFit: Carmen is Bizet's opera, set in Seville.

clue.text: Second smuggler brought before the court?

parts.note: a runner, as in gunrunner or rum-runner, smuggles goods
to be up before a magistrate is to be in court

explanation.surface: Another smuggler is arraigned.
explanation.definitionFit: The one finishing second in a race is the runner-up.

clue.text: Be a dog — work out in the wine bar!

indicators.note: work out says the letters are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Behave like a hound and exercise in the tavern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work out' reads as exercise but rearranges BE A DOG.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodega is a Spanish wine shop or bar.

clue.text: Put off certain players

definitions.meaning: to ... off is to shed or discard, as a snake ... its skin
the actors in a particular play make up its ...

explanation.definitionFit: To shed or throw away, and the company of actors in a production.

clue.text: Some investors describe risk-taking as a bloomer

indicators.note: some says only part of the run of letters is taken

explanation.surface: Investors call gambling a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests a mistake, but it is a flower. The run sits across 'describe' and 'risk'.
explanation.definitionFit: Iberis, candytuft, is a garden flowering plant.

clue.text: Barely used pied-a terre in the West Country?

parts.note: Bath is a city in Somerset, in England's West Country
a pied-a-terre is a small lodging, here a room

explanation.surface: A rarely occupied flat in the West of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barely' means naked here, not hardly; the room in Bath is the BATH plus ROOM.
explanation.definitionFit: A room where one is unclothed, used while undressed.

clue.text: Oriental combine that's come to light

parts.note: E, east, stands for Oriental
to merge is to combine

explanation.surface: An Eastern conglomerate has been exposed.
explanation.definitionFit: To emerge is to appear or become known, to surface.

clue.text: He looks after the stock, but' not mares, oddly enough

indicators.note: oddly enough signals the letters fall into a strange new order

explanation.surface: A stockman who tends cattle but not horses, curiously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stock' suggests livestock beside 'mares', but it is goods in a store.
explanation.definitionFit: A storeman is in charge of the stores, the goods held in stock.
